title: Typography scale for headings and text
when: The user wants consistent font sizes, heading sizes or a type system for a page or app.
inputs: density: reading site or compact app
prompt:
Goal: A modular type scale of 6 to 8 steps with matched line heights and weights, used for every text on the page.
Steps:
1. Set body at 1rem and never set the html font-size in px, so the user font setting still works.
2. Choose a ratio: 1.2 for dense apps, 1.25 for general sites, 1.333 for editorial pages.
3. Multiply out the steps; for 1.25: 0.8, 1, 1.25, 1.563, 1.953, 2.441, 3.052 rem.
4. Store them as --step--1 to --step-5 on :root; map h1 to --step-5 down to h6, small print to --step--1.
5. Set line-height by size: 1.5 to 1.6 body, 1.2 to 1.3 headings, 1.1 display.
6. Limit weights to 400, 600 and 700; add letter-spacing (0.05em) only to all caps labels.
Quality bar:
- Smallest text at least 12 px, body at least 16 px.
- Each heading level is visibly larger or bolder than the next.
- Sizes in rem so zoom scales them.
Pitfalls:
- A dozen ad hoc sizes like 13, 15 and 17 px.
- Headings that wrap to five lines on phones.
- Body line-height under 1.4.
Verify:
- [ ] Every font-size uses a scale variable.
- [ ] No size below 12 px.
- [ ] Headings follow the scale in order.
- [ ] Line heights set per role.
Output: The scale on :root and base typography rules (body, h1 to h6, small) in style.css.

examples.input: organize os tamanhos de fonte do meu blog
examples.output: ratio 1.25: --step-0 1rem body, --step-5 3.05rem h1, line-height 1.6 body and 1.2 headings
